title: Checking for Extraneous Solutions
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: Algebraic transformations can sometimes introduce invalid candidates or remove valid solutions. Checking the original equation protects against these errors.

content.text: Checking is especially important after squaring, multiplying by expressions, dividing by expressions, or using reciprocal functions.
Substitute each candidate back into the original equation rather than checking only a transformed version.

examples.question: Why should a solution obtained after squaring both sides be checked?
examples.solution: Squaring can make two expressions equal even when their original signs were different. Therefore a candidate must be substituted into the original equation.

key_ideas: Check candidates after transformations that may change the solution set.
The original equation is the final authority.
misconceptions: Assuming every algebraically obtained value is automatically valid.
